{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that the intervention training would improve the time until the first hit in shoot scenarios compared to the control group.",
  "design": "mixed, 2 (group: intervention vs. control) x 2 (measurement time: pre-test vs. post-test)",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "An individual video-based police firearms training intervention based on the Four-Component Instructional Design Model (4C/ID), focusing on situational awareness, tactical gaze control, and visual attention, compared to an active control training resembling traditional police firearms training.",
  "outcome_measure": "Time until the first hit (in milliseconds) in realistic shoot/don't shoot video scenarios, measured as the time between the detection of the black handgun and the first effective hit in predefined areas.",
  "population_and_setting": "45 senior police officers recruited from the German Police University, tested in an indoor firing range lab setting.",
  "sample_size_total": 45,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited via notices on campus; participation was voluntary; debriefed at the end of the study.",
  "analysis_plan": "Repeated measures ANOVA with the within-subject factor Time and the between-subject factor Group.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "preregistered",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants used a gas-operated replica of a Heckler and Koch SFP9 handgun. Eye-tracking glasses were used during testing. Exclusions were applied for wearers of glasses, weapon malfunctions, false negative decisions, and failure to hit predefined areas."
}
